def bachgold_problem(n):
    # Helper function to generate all primes up to n using the Sieve of Eratosthenes
    def sieve_of_eratosthenes(limit):
        is_prime = [True] * (limit + 1)
        p = 2
        while (p * p <= limit):
            if (is_prime[p] == True):
                for i in range(p * p, limit + 1, p):
                    is_prime[i] = False
            p += 1
        prime_numbers = [p for p in range(2, limit + 1) if is_prime[p]]
        return prime_numbers

    # Generate all primes up to n
    primes = sieve_of_eratosthenes(n)

    # Dynamic programming approach to find the maximum number of primes that sum up to n
    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    prime_used = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]

    for prime in primes:
        for i in range(prime, n + 1):
            if dp[i] < dp[i - prime] + 1:
                dp[i] = dp[i - prime] + 1
                prime_used[i] = prime_used[i - prime] + [prime]

    # Output the result
    print(dp[n])
    print(" ".join(map(str, prime_used[n])))
